newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gold Fields not in mining talks with Nail.
newsitem.headline: Gold Fields not in mining talks with Nail.

text.p: Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd said on Thursday that black empowerment business group New Africa Investments Ltd (Nail) had been speaking to it but not about taking a stake in the group's mining operations.
"They have been speaking to us but we have not been in negotiations about a sale in mining," said Alan Munro, Gold Fields' chief executive of gold operations.
Asked about Nail deputy executive chairman Cyril Ramaphosa's statement that his group was not interested in acquiring Gold Fields, Munro said:
"He is a sensible man and if a sensible man got the chance to have a controlling stake in Gold Fields, he would jump at it."

Ramaphosa was quoted by the local Business Report newspaper on Monday as saying: "I deny emphatically that we are interested in Gold Fields. We don't want Gold Fields. We are once bitten, twice shy about gold."

He was responding to a report in the British Financial Times which said he and Rembrandt Group chairman Johann Rupert had held long discussions about plans to take black investors on board as Gold Fields investors.
Rembrandt has a pivotal role in control of the mining house.
A consortium led by Nail last year lost a bid for Anglo American Corp of South Africa's stake in another mining house, JCI Ltd.
